_meta.what: The ONE reader-facing vocabulary + gloss registry (#4182 ruling vii, 2026-09-26; #4035's acronym registry folded in from the retired site/config/glossary.json). Every builder term that reaches a reader page's MAIN content is listed with its ruling; every term a reader may need defined carries a `match` and a `gloss`. Consumers: scripts/v4_glossary.py (build-time <dfn class="gloss"> on each glossed term's first eligible appearance per page, via scripts/v4_apply_chrome.py), site/assets/js/glossary_terms.js (GENERATED by `v4_glossary.py --emit-js` — the runtime pass gloss_runtime.js uses for JS-rendered text), tests/test_site_vocabulary_registry.py (the ruled terms' shrink-only ratchet) and tests/test_glossary_4035.py (the two-sided gloss gate). Charter primitives 1+2: this file owns the vocabulary; nothing else may hand-list it.

rulings.rename: the reader-facing word changes to reader_form; URLs, code identifiers and /method/* keep the term
rulings.cut: the term leaves reader pages (it may stay on /method/* and in essays)
rulings.keep-with-gloss: the term stays; its first use on every reader page carries the gloss inline (a <dfn title>)

_meta.panel: Product Board personas + four stand-ins, red-teamed 2026-09-26; dissent in docs/SITE_TRANSFORMATION_V6.md §9

match.exact: case-sensitive, word-bounded — acronyms (HRV, DEXA, …) and proper names
match.word-ci: case-insensitive, word-bounded — everyday words kept with a gloss (cockpit, cycle, …); skipped inside a/button/h1/h2/code/label
match.(absent): not glossed by the build — a rename/cut ruling is a copy pass, not a tooltip

kinds.acronym: #4035's newcomer glossary — no vocabulary ruling, so no ledger row; glossed wherever it appears

Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry — the periodic full-body scan behind the body-composition numbers (fat mass, lean mass, bone density).
Continuous glucose monitor — a worn sensor that reads blood glucose every few minutes instead of one fingerstick at a time.
Rapid eye movement — the sleep stage associated with dreaming and memory consolidation, one of the stages sleep trackers report.
Architecture decision record — a dated, numbered document explaining why the platform's engine is built a certain way.
Large language model — the AI model class (Claude, via AWS Bedrock) behind the platform's coaching narratives and this glossary's own build.
Model Context Protocol — the interface that lets an AI assistant query this platform's own data directly, tool by tool.
Experience points — the character sheet's leveling currency, earned from real daily pillar scores, not from playing a game.
False discovery rate — the statistical correction applied so a batch of correlation tests isn't overstated by chance.
Brier score — a 0 (perfect) to 1 (worst) grade for how well a forecast's stated probability matched what actually happened.
Exponentially weighted moving average — a running average that counts recent days more than older ones, so a trend reacts to change without chasing one noisy day.
